speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: And just before or just after they enter the workforce, they can tap on schemes like the Global Ready Talent Programme to study and work overseas.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: They will gain valuable real-world skills and insights from foreign markets, to support their career aspirations.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: This is in fact, something that MOE has been doing for years.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: However, even with excellent pre-employment education, our workers will need to be proactive about upskilling and reskilling.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: The new economy will require workers who are versatile and know how to build on existing skills, embrace lifelong learning, and be able to move between adjacent industry clusters.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: But upskilling is not the responsibility of workers alone.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: They should actively participate in the development of training programmes, redesign jobs, and encourage employees to upskill.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: As Ms Jessica Tan rightly pointed out, training should be demand-led to ensure industry relevance.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: And Ms Foo Mee Har has just proposed an IST, Industry Skills Training.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Ms Poh Li San also suggested meeting the needs of the manufacturing sector.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Indeed, there is a very wide range of labour market issues – the demand for labour, the supply of labour, the changing labour profile, the way that we can more effectively match jobs and skills, and how we can develop the right skills profile and the right jobs profile to meet the needs and aspirations of our people.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: These are issues that we will continue to study but we will provide strong support to our workers and firms.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: The National Silver Academy offers a wide range of subsidised courses, from Starting a Home Business to Taking Care of the Aged.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: With the Retirement and Re-employment Ages set to be raised by 2022, those who want to continue working can choose to do so.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: With these efforts, we hope that Singaporeans, regardless of age, can continue to learn and upskill so that they not only have good jobs, but experience good wage growth.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: These efforts to upskill our workforce will help us to stay ahead of the global curve.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Coupled with openness to ideas, innovations and innovators, we secure a brighter future.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: As a global city, our economic competition and collaboration are with other global cities like New York, London, Frankfurt, Shanghai and Mumbai.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: These cities have their own hinterlands and can draw talent from millions and billions of their own nationals.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: In Singapore, we draw from a domestic population of about four million locals.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: As Ms Joan Pereira has aptly put, "a Singapore that closes its doors to the outside world is bad for all of us".

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: As the global economy undergoes changes driven by technology and innovation, it is even more critical that we assemble the best possible team to stay useful and relevant to the world.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We want to make sure that we have the best players in our team, playing to one another’s strengths, working together as a team.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: This is why we must remain open to the best talents from all over the world, so that we can put forth the best team and step out onto the world stage.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: By bringing the best to our shores, we learn from them and synthesise good ideas from around the world.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Our scientific community, for example, has gained from the diversity of exceptional minds that have come to call Singapore their home.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Leading researchers Prof Sir David Lane and Prof Birgit Lane have provided thought leadership that has spurred our advancements in the biomedical sciences.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: The late Nobel Laureate Dr Sydney Brenner was also a giant in the global scientific community, who helped us set up the Institute of Molecular and Cell Biology (IMCB) in 1985.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Today, IMCB is a world recognised biology institution.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We also send our best minds overseas to learn from others.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Mr Philip Yeo, former chairman of A*STAR, started the A*STAR scholarship with the hope of grooming outstanding Singaporeans in science and technology.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We have since awarded more than 1,500 scholarships to some of our best students, and many are now back in Singapore with a global network and contributing significantly in our R&D efforts.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Our openness has also allowed our locals to collaborate with the best.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: The Cooling Singapore 2.0 programme facilitated by the National Research Foundation has brought together an international team of researchers from our local universities and researchers from ETH Zurich.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: This joint team is working with our public agencies to develop new modelling and simulation models to support our urban planning and policy-making.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: A good complement of foreign students and researchers in our universities have also made good nests for innovations that are going global.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: For example, Pedra Technology is a deep tech medical start-up that came out of NTU’s labs.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Its founders are a Korean, two Singaporeans and a UK citizen born in India.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: This diversity will put them in good stead to expand into these different markets.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: As a global city competing and collaborating with other global cities, it is crucial that we remain open and at the same time, invest in our people.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: That way, we remain relevant and useful to the world.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We must take care of our people and build a cohesive and resilient society.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Several Members spoke about the need to continue supporting our households, especially the lower income, through this crisis.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: This is the largest amount we have ever disbursed in a single year.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: All Singaporean households, regardless of property type, have received relief in some form, with lower and middle income households receiving higher levels of support from the Care and Support Package.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: More support was provided for lower income households.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: In addition to household transfers, we have also introduced the Community Development Council or CDC Vouchers Scheme to help households in need with their daily expenses, while supporting local hawkers and heartland merchants.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: There are now more than 8,000 merchants on board.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: As of September 2020, more than 300,000 Singaporean households have benefited from the first tranche of the CDC voucher scheme.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Mr Ang Wei Neng will be pleased to note that we intend to disburse a second tranche over the next few months.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Ms He Ting Ru spoke passionately about supporting the needs of young families.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: To ease the financial concerns that couples may have about starting a family in the near-term, we have also announced a one-off Baby Support Grant of $3,000 for each child born from 1 October 2020 to 31 September 2022.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Minister Indranee has earlier addressed some of the concerns raised by Members, so I will not dwell further on this.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: I hope all this support has gone some way to help our households alleviate the impact brought about by COVID-19.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: As part of our efforts to build a cohesive society, we must also ensure that vulnerable groups are not left behind.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: I agree with Dr Wan Rizal and Ms Hany Soh on being digitally inclusive, especially for our seniors.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: To support our seniors, IMDA launched the Seniors Go Digital movement in May 2020 to encourage seniors to equip them with digital skills.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: I also agree with Mr Melvin Yong and Ms Raeesah Khan that mental health is a rising concern, especially during this COVID-19 period.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: As one of the initiatives under the Singapore Together Action Networks, we have also set up the Youth Mental Well-being (YMWB) Network.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: This allows anyone who is interested in improving the mental health of young people to contribute, kickstart discussions and take ownership of the projects.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Building a cohesive society requires the effort of not just the Government alone, but of all Singaporeans together.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: COVID-19 has shown how far we have come as a community, as a society, and how resilient we are as a people.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Many of us have contributed and even made personal sacrifices in our fight against COVID-19.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: This is why we are in a more stable position today.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: I am glad that there continues to be many ground-up community movements to help those in need.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: For example, KampungKakis, a neighbourhood buddy system to support the elderly, low-income families and vulnerable residents during the COVID-19 crisis.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Volunteer kakis were the additional eyes and ears of our grassroot leader, who guided their kakis-in-need to available resources and ensured vulnerable residents received assistance.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Our Social Service Agencies have also been working tirelessly to support those who need a helping hand.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: To support these efforts, we have the Enhanced Fundraising Programme to provide dollar-for-dollar matching for some charities.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: This is in addition to enhanced tax deductions for donations to charities with IPC status.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: I am also heartened that donations for COVID-19 related causes have remained resilient.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: This is already more than the overall donations received by the Community Chest and Giving.sg throughout 2019.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: I encourage those who can to continue donating generously.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: And as Mr Ang Wei Neng suggested, companies can donate their JSS payouts to worthy causes.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: For instance, Lockheed Martin has donated their JSS payouts to The Invictus Fund and The Courage Fund.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: For those who have donated, I thank you for your contributions.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: This is the spirit of SG Together in action – a community of deeds, where we support one another, combine our various strengths, and make sure no one is left behind.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: I mentioned earlier that Singapore is both a global city and a nation.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: As a nation, we have spending priorities that cities do not have.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Yet unlike other cities, we do not have a federal government to bail us out.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: As a nation, our planning horizon cannot be just 10, 20 or even 50 years like a company or an individual.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We have to think about the countless generations that come after us.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: This is why it is critical that we remain fiscally prudent, to make sure that we spend within our means, and also leave something behind for future Singaporeans.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: For this latest Fifth Support Package, we are able to fund it entirely from Budget reallocation.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: As mentioned in my Ministerial Statement earlier, our guiding principle is prudence, not austerity.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: The Government did an extensive scan, Ministry by Ministry, to identify deferment or reductions in expenditure.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Some expenditures such as those for MRT lines, HDB upgrading, and sewerage and drainage works were deferred arising from delays due to the circuit breaker and the safe re-opening of the construction sector thereafter.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Some expenditures were also lower than earlier projected due to COVID-19 and safe distancing measures.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: However, most of these are not savings but delayed spending which will still be incurred in future years as Mr Liang Eng Hwa has rightly pointed out.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Mr Xie Yao Quan suggested that we should not delay critical projects.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Indeed, for projects that are critically important, we will resume these.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: These projects are needed to raise Singaporeans’ standard of living and our economic development.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We will push ahead when the conditions allow.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We are also already reviewing major infrastructure projects to account for the longer term impact of COVID-19.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: For example, the construction of Changi Airport Terminal 5 has been put on hold for two years amid uncertainties over how COVID-19 will change the aviation sector.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: There could be further deferments or reductions in scale, if demand takes longer to recover.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Conversely, we may also need to build in more resilience and safety features, which could raise project costs.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Mr Liang Eng Hwa asked how we would balance our Budget.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: In fact, looking ahead, our fiscal situation will get tighter.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Our revenues in the medium term are expected to be subdued and uncertain for two reasons.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: First, global economic growth will likely remain weakened for several years.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Second, we can expect global competition for tax revenue to intensify.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Many advanced economies have accumulated more debt to fund their COVID-19 responses, which they will need to repay.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: There is added impetus globally to push for "re-allocation" of taxing rights under the Base Erosion and Profit Shifting project, or BEPS in short.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: So, even as we contend with these revenue challenges, we cannot lose sight of our goal to secure the long-term needs of Singapore.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: As I have shared on multiple occasions, we expect expenditure to increase in public healthcare and pre-school education.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: This is vital to ensuring we can take better care of our old and young.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: In order for Singapore to continue thriving as a global city tomorrow, we must ensure our financial security as a nation today.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We are therefore making the responsible decision today, to study how we can strengthen our fiscal toolkit.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Even before COVID-19 struck, we have explained that we are looking into borrowing for major long-term infrastructure.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: This will help to spread out the hefty upfront costs equitably across current and future generations who will benefit from such investments.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Our approach will be a principled and prudent one.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We will borrow only for infrastructure that benefit multiple generations, and ensure that our debt level and future repayments are sustainable.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: I am glad that Mr Louis Chua echoed our stance to maintain a disciplined use of borrowing for projects that will benefit multiple generations of Singaporeans We will not borrow just to make up for revenue shortfalls or be opportunistic in timing the market.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: However, for recurrent spending like healthcare and education that benefits the current generations, the responsible way is to pay for them using what we earn, through recurrent revenues like taxes.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: This discipline ensures that every generation earns and pays its share.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Several Members have asked about the timing of the GST rate increase.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: However, we cannot defer the GST rate increase indefinitely.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: The GST rate increase is to support our future needs in healthcare and pre-school education.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We will continue to study the timing of increasing the GST rate carefully, taking into account the pace of our economic recovery, our revenue outlook and how much spending we can defer to later years, without jeopardising our long-term needs.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Ms Foo Mee Har asked if our assumptions behind the GST rate increase have been affected by COVID-19.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We expect collections to continue to be lower than usual until international travel recovers fully, which we expect to be at least a couple of years away.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: On top of the transitional support, we have the permanent GST Voucher scheme, which will be enhanced to provide more help to lower income households and seniors.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: I would also like to point out that over 60% of the GST borne by all individuals and households is from foreigners residing in Singapore, tourists and the top 20% of resident households.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Mr Leong Mun Wai's suggestions to shelf the GST rate increase indefinitely means that we lose the additional revenues from this group which we can use to improve the lives of Singaporeans.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: I do not know if Mr Leong is aware of this.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: And as what Mr Murali Pillai has just showed us in a chart earlier, our fiscal support is very significant, very significant for Singapore and very significant compared to many other countries.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: And we did not incur a cent of debt to fund our package.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: This is unlike many other countries, which had to borrow further to fund their COVID-19 response, despite already being at high levels of debt.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: In Singapore, we are fortunate to have a rainy-day fund built up over the generations that has allowed us to mount a quick and strong response.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We are drawing up to $52 billion from our past reserves to fund the support packages.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Several Members have asked for clarifications on this $52 billion draw.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Mr Louis Chua asked how the draw on reserves would impact the Net Investment Returns Contribution or NIRC.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Yes, there will be some impact to NIRC but the design of the NIR framework is to provide a stable, sustainable source of income to our Budget, smoothed out over market cycles.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: This means that when the projected returns and value of the net asset base goes down, we do not see an immediate proportionate decrease in NIRC.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: In the same way, in periods of sharp spikes in the market and asset values go up, we do not see an immediate increase and overspend.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Mr Gerald Giam asked about the Government's plans to put back the sums drawn from our reserves.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Mr Leong Mun Wai has suggested the amount of reserves drawn is much less than $52 billion and he has cited several figures in his speech.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: I will not repeat his computation but I will just make two points.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: First, the NIR framework is based on expected long-term returns, not actual returns.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: So, it is incorrect to estimate the actual return by multiplying the NIRC by two.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Second, in considering the amount that we are spending from our reserves, it is wrong to subtract the returns from the $52 billion to derive a net spending figure.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: In addition to the draw, we continue to spend NIRC which also comes from our reserves.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: And furthermore, the amount drawn from the reserves would have generated returns in perpetuity without a draw.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: So, the draw of $52 billion is unprecedented and no one should downplay its size or significance.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: The COVID-19 pandemic has shown us how our reserves allowed us to remain nimble in times of uncertainty.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: When I delivered the Unity Budget in February, we did not foresee a need to draw on our Past Reserves.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: In fact, Mr Pritam Singh said at the debate then that the Government had, and I quote, "the privilege of far more budgetary elbow room, both political and fiscal, than any previous government in Singapore's history." In the short span of 100 days since the Unity Budget when Mr Singh made these remarks, we have delivered three more Budgets and had to propose a draw of up to $52 billion from our Past Reserves to help save lives and livelihoods.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Therefore, as you can see, we face great uncertainties.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: It is too early to conclude that we have unlimited space.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: So, we need to be more circumspect when it comes to using more reserves, as we are confronted with greater uncertainties ahead.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: First, the global economy and financial system will be more volatile.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: The build-up of debt globally introduces instability in the financial system, which can lead to or exacerbate crises.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Second, we are seeing increasing risk of geopolitical conflicts and deglobalisation.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Third, scientists have warned of the risk of another serious international epidemic caused by a new unknown disease, Disease X.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: As long as Singapore continues to exist, the question is not whether there will be an externally induced crisis but when.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: If we spend more or even all the returns from our reserves annually, future generations will likely have a smaller buffer in a world of greater uncertainty.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We must therefore ensure that we continue to spend within our means and hand over to our children more than what we have inherited from our previous generations.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Mr Liang Eng Hwa asked whether the Government would consider a further draw on reserves, considering the magnitude and severity of this crisis.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Indeed, there is profound uncertainty in this trajectory of this pandemic and its economic impact.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We must act early and decisively to support our workers and businesses when needed.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: So, I am prepared to propose to the President a further draw on our Past Reserves should it be necessary for us to do so.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: In the medium to longer term, our approach is to adapt and find new ways to generate growth.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We must work hard to get ourselves back in a position where our economy is growing and we can build up reserves for the future again.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: This is the sustainable and prudent way forward.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: This COVID-19 crisis is a test of how far we have come as a global city and a nation.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: How we respond will determine how far we will go.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Singapore's dual identity as both a city and a nation has given us agency, nimbleness and unique strengths.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: But it has also conferred upon us some unique challenges which we have turned into successes.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: In the face of new threats and opportunities, we must continue to stay open as a global city yet closely-knit as one people and one nation.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Over the next few months, we will continue to study ways to help our businesses and people emerge stronger.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Our consultations for Budget 2021 have already begun.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: The Emerging Stronger Taskforce is pressing on with the Alliances for Action to seize growth opportunities for Singapore, even as we deal with COVID-19.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: I have also set up teams to look into how we can better support workers and households in the post-COVID-19 world.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Our battle with COVID-19 is far from over and the road ahead in a post-COVID-19 world will be uncertain.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: But I am confident that if we stay open and stay united, we will continue thriving as an exciting and vibrant global city and emerge stronger as a more cohesive and resilient nation.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: And most important of all, we must retain our core values.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: It has been a test of a generation, which we have tackled as one nation.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: The Government has rolled out a decisive set of crisis management measures to minimise and cushion economic impact, preserve jobs and capabilities, and support households.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: This includes the support measures which I announced in August, before the Opening of Parliament.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: I made the announcement then, as some of the support schemes were ending in August and we needed to give our firms and workers certainty during this difficult period.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We are now tabling a Supplementary Supply Bill, which provides for the resources to implement the measures announced in August, for debate in Parliament.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: My Ministerial Statement today will provide context for the Supplementary Supply Bill.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: This is on top of other measures such as special relief measures for debtors and tenants.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: These measures have substantially cushioned the economic impact.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: This outcome has only been possible with the collective determination, adaptability and sacrifice of our people and businesses.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Today, I want to look forward, and share how we will approach the next six months as our economy reopens, as well as our plans for our longer term economic recovery to emerge stronger.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: The trajectory of our economic recovery depends critically on how well the world deals with this still dangerous virus.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Every passing day brings new surprises and new hope.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Even as we learn more about it, there are profound uncertainties ahead.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: One major uncertainty is how effective other countries are in containing the pandemic and the success of policies they adopt in opening their economies.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Another key uncertainty is whether, and when, an effective and safe vaccine can be developed.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Even if such a vaccine becomes available, the pandemic may not end quickly.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Supply of the vaccine will be limited initially, and global rollout is likely to be uneven.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We do not know how long the protective effect may last, or if mutation of the virus may render it ineffective.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: But there is also hope that we can overcome this crisis.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: In our fight against COVID-19, we are currently in a stable position, but we must remain vigilant.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Amid the uncertainties, we are adapting to living with the virus.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We have worked out the steps to further re-open safely in the months ahead.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We are putting ourselves in the best position to fight COVID-19 by focusing on four key prongs.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We are working very actively to secure early access to safe and effective vaccines, if and when they become available.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Singapore is an early supporter of the COVID-19 Vaccine Global Access or COVAX Facility, which accelerates the development and production of, and equitable access to potential COVID-19 vaccines.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Together with Switzerland, Singapore co-chairs the Friends of the COVAX Facility to promote vaccine multi-lateralisation.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Singapore is also pursuing the procurement of COVID-19 vaccines with a number of pharmaceutical companies.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: At the same time, we are supporting local efforts to develop a COVID-19 vaccine as well as building up vaccine manufacturing capacity.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: In the meantime, we have increased our Polymerase Chain Reaction or PCR testing capacity manifold, and are close to our target of being able to conduct 40,000 laboratory tests a day.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We are also evaluating new testing technologies that are less invasive and can produce test results more quickly.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: This enhanced testing capability will help us safely resume more activities sooner.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Swift contact tracing and isolation of infected individuals are key to limiting the spread of the virus.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Our contact tracing teams are doing a sterling job and using digital tools well.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: The TraceTogether app, together with tokens that are being distributed nationwide, and the SafeEntry programme, enable contact tracing to reach the speed and coverage needed to rapidly contain viral transmission.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We must continue to adhere to safe management measures and do our part to facilitate contact tracing.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Keeping community infections low is the key to re-opening our economy safely.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: The Multi-Ministry Task force co-chaired by Ministers Gan Kim Yong and Lawrence Wong will be releasing more details on the roadmap to Phase Three in the coming weeks.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: This will include the expected timeline for moving to Phase Three, changes to current regulations on the size of group gatherings, and participation at mass events.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: While managing the healthcare front of the COVID-19 battle, we must also deal with economic and social fronts.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Many of our businesses, workers, and households have been hit hard by the disruptions and uncertainties due to COVID-19.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Our path to recovery will not be easy.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Our support over the four Budgets has been to provide immediate relief and also to minimise the scarring effects of COVID-19 on our economy, by preparing our businesses and workers to emerge stronger.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: In short, we are working together to alleviate near-term pains to build for a better tomorrow.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We will remain focused on these over the next six months and beyond.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: With the situation stabilising in Singapore and some parts of the world, we will progressively open up more activities, at a pace that enables new practices to be internalised, to keep everyone safe.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: The performance and outlook for different economic sectors is highly uneven.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Some sectors are doing better than before COVID-19.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Firms in the IT, biomedical, e-commerce and finance sectors have benefited from the rise in demand for these services during this period.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Some restaurants and hawkers are on their way to recovery.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Construction activities will gradually resume as we complete the testing of workers and as they adjust to new safe management measures.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: But sectors that involve the movement of people across borders, such as aviation and tourism, will recover only when people around the world feel safe enough to resume travel and this will take some time.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: And businesses that involve large gatherings, such as in MICE, sports and concerts, will recover slowly, unless rapid test kits are effective in screening participants for safe entry.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Not only are the outlooks different for different sectors, but within sectors, firms that have been nimble are doing better.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: For instance, some wet market stalls started online selling, and are enjoying robust business.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Given these differences in outlook between and within sectors, we have adjusted broad-based wage support under JSS.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: For the hardest-hit sectors such as aviation and tourism, which face an uncertain road to recovery, our aim is to help companies preserve core capabilities and enable workers to retain specialised skills.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: As earlier announced in August, this will be through the Enhanced Aviation Support Package, a temporary redeployment programme, and the SingapoRediscovers Vouchers.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: In tandem, we will continue to provide strong support to firms that are growing.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: In this way, our workers can move into growth areas, stay employed, and build new skills.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We have enhanced support for start-ups, via the Startup SG Founder programme.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Since I announced the enhancements in August, more than 500 aspiring entrepreneurs have signed up for the three-month Venture Building programmes.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We will provide wage support of between 25% and 50% for each new local hire in firms which increase their total local headcount, through the Jobs Growth Incentive, or JGI.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: The support will be for the first $5,000 of gross monthly wages for up to 12 months.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: This will apply to new hires of Persons with Disabilities from September 2020 to February 2021.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: To give a boost to businesses seeking to internationalise, transform and digitalise, I will extend or enhance our capability-building grants, namely the Market Readiness Assistance Grant, the Productivity Solutions Grant, the Enterprise Development Grant, and the PACT programme.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: These will enable firms to tap on new sources of growth.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: MTI will announce details in the coming weeks.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Even as we shift our approach in supporting businesses and workers as the economy recovers, we will make sure that the support does not taper off too sharply.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We had earlier enhanced support through loan schemes to provide working capital support for viable businesses.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We will extend the Temporary Bridging Loan Programme for six months, until September 2021, at reduced levels.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: MAS will also extend the MAS Singapore Dollar Facility for Enterprise Singapore Loans, until September 2021.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We will adjust the support available under the Enterprise Financing Scheme to help Singapore enterprises access financing in areas such as trade and project needs.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: MTI and MAS will announce more details later.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Later today, MAS will be announcing details on the extension of payment moratoriums, at a tapered level of support.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Taken together, the staging of these measures avoids sharp drops in support, while facilitating restructuring where needed.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: All this support for our firms will ultimately benefit our workers.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: The best way to protect the welfare of our workers is a good job.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: By helping viable firms stay afloat during this difficult period, they can retain their workers.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: By helping firms to restructure and retrain their workers, they can emerge stronger.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: More competitive and productive firms can provide better jobs and better prospects for workers.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: And more skilled and committed workers make firms more competitive.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: This synergy between competitive firms and capable workers is critical for both to do well.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: As part of our long-standing practice of tripartism, we must not fear, but instead ride on change together to achieve synergies and to emerge stronger.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: But even with the best efforts, some firms, especially in hardest hit sectors, may not survive, or may have to release some of their workers.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: So, other than supporting workers through our firms, we will continue to provide our fullest support to workers who have lost their jobs, to help them reskill and move into firms that are hiring.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: The National Jobs Council is implementing the SGUnited Jobs and Skills Package that I announced at the Fortitude Budget in May.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: This is good progress, but we must press on.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: The Council is working closely with companies to hire mid-career jobseekers looking to make a switch in their careers and to redeploy workers in affected sectors where activities are low, such as aviation and tourism, to areas of need and where their skills are valued, such as healthcare and childcare.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: It is also engaging companies to offer traineeships, company attachments and training opportunities, which can later lead to good jobs.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: The Singapore Business Federation, or SBF, is working closely with other TACs and NTUC’s e2i to do business-to-business job matching across sectors, through the SBF SGUnited Jobs Initiative.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: MOM and WSG will also be appointing employment agencies as Placement Partners, to assist in placements.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: I encourage everyone to step out of your comfort zones and keep an open mind to learn new skills and take on new jobs.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: One good example is Ms Tan Bee Lian, who is preparing to be a Healthcare Assistant after being in the oil and gas industry for over 30 years.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Beyond this year, we are studying the support for self-employed persons and workers who are most vulnerable.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: The continuation and form of support will depend on the labour market situation and economic outlook.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: One key consideration is to make a stronger link to helping individuals find a new job or to acquire new skills.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: In this way, we can better prepare our displaced workers for new opportunities as firms restructure.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We will provide an update before the end of the year.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Other than supporting our businesses and workers, we will also continue to support our households.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: The household support announced earlier continues to flow in the coming months.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Please refer to this slide on schedule of support measures, which will also be digitally distributed to Members after the session.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: In it, you will notice that in October alone, eligible households will receive the GST Voucher – U-Save, the first tranche of Grocery Vouchers, and Service and Conservancy Charges, or S&CC, rebates.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Eligible lower income workers will also receive the October tranche of Workfare Special Payment.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We have received feedback that COVID-19 has caused some aspiring parents to postpone their parenthood plans.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: This will be on top of the Baby Bonus Cash Gift, which provides eligible parents up to $10,000 in benefits.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Minister Indranee will share more details on the additional support soon.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: I have laid out our approach to support our firms, workers and households in dealing with COVID-19 in the next six months and to have more babies.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We will adjust our support if necessary, in response to changes on the medical front and global economic developments.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: I hope that businesses, workers and households will make good use of these resources in the months ahead.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Beyond the immediate crisis, we want to emerge from COVID-19 stronger as a society and more united as a people.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We are determined to have better jobs for our workers and stronger support to enable them to bounce back if they fall.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We want to build an endearing home for future generations, and a fair and caring society based on what we stand for as a people.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: To deliver on these priorities, we need a dynamic and growing economy, with good jobs for all Singaporeans.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Economic growth is an enabler for individuals and families to realise their aspirations and ensures that the public sector is adequately resourced to invest in our national priorities.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Given the importance of economic growth as an enabler, I will now spend some time to sketch out the broad strokes of our strategy.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Our future economy must be responsive to structural shifts, many of which have been accelerated by COVID-19.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Support for globalisation is weakening and some countries are turning inwards.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: The adoption of digital technology has been given renewed impetus, unlocking new sources of return.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Digital technology and its many applications are the new capital of the innovation-driven future economy.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Asia continues to rise in global economic weight, as its recovery accelerates.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Ensuring sustainability and care for the environment are gaining momentum.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: At home, we face slowing resident labour force growth.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Future economic growth will come from raising productivity across the economy.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: So, we must make the best use of the skills and talents of our people and use new technology as a key complement.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We are at a critical juncture in our economic development and the stakes are high.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: In the next few years, economies will undergo rapid transitions.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Depending on their response, COVID-19 will benefit some and disadvantage others, whether at the firm-level, sector-level, or across the entire economy.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We must take the actions now that will allow us to not just get through COVID-19, but more crucially, gain ground that will pave the way for our next lap of economic growth in the next five to 10 years.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: I will speak on what we are preparing for in this next lap of growth.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Before I get into the details, I wish to stress that everything this Government does to protect, re-open, and grow our economy – we do, not for the economy’s sake, but for our people.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We strive to secure a way for Singapore to continue to make a good living, so that Singaporeans can have a good life.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Since 2017, the Future Economy Council has been driving the implementation of our Industry Transformation Maps, or ITMs, to restructure our economy sector by sector, firm by firm.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: This is also an improvement over the 2.2% per year growth in the preceding three-year period.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Incomes at the 20th percentile grew by 4.4% per year in the past three years, up from 4% in the preceding three years.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: In 2015, we launched the SkillsFuture movement as well as our Research, Innovation and Enterprise, or RIE 2020 plan.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: These support our ITM work by strengthening our foundations of skills and innovation.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We are building on our good position and keeping up the pace.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: In the midst of this pandemic, we set up the Emerging Stronger Taskforce in May to update our economic roadmap to respond to the new realities and to emerge with a new competitive edge.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: There are many new business and growth opportunities for Singapore to seize, and the Taskforce has already made significant progress in this through the Alliances for Action.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: As rapid-action taskforces, the seven Alliances have rallied key players around common challenges faced by industry.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: They are developing prototypes to validate new business ideas, new business models, and new business solutions, in areas such as sustainability, robotics, and safe visitor experiences.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Government agencies are partnering businesses to review regulations and promote innovation.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Beyond the first wave of Alliances, the Taskforce is looking to launch new Alliances to build momentum for change and explore opportunities in new areas of growth, such as MedTech.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: All these moves build on our ITM framework to deliver a refreshed economic strategy for a post-COVID-19 world, with emphasis on three priority areas.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: First, remaking Singapore as a Global-Asia node of technology, innovation, and enterprise.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We will secure our external economic linkages as a vital global node in Asia and transform ourselves into a vibrant centre of technology and innovation.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Second, redoubling our efforts to foster inclusive growth.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: With COVID-19 revealing vulnerabilities in our labour market, we need to better understand its structure, and upgrade jobs and skills across all segments of society.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Third, investing in economic resilience and sustainability as a source of competitive advantage.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Our resilience can be a source of growth, at many levels – for our individuals, industries, nation, and the world.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: COVID-19 has changed travel patterns, sharpened the fragmentation of supply chains and accelerated digitalisation in different markets.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: It has heightened emphasis on resilience as companies and countries review their operations.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Asia, in particular Southeast Asia, will continue to grow as one of the key global engines.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We must deepen and broaden links to build up Singapore’s role at the heart of Asia’s growth, while forging connectivity with other key markets.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: A role that we have played in our long history as a trading port and which we will renew in two ways: one, rebuild and grow our physical connectivity – in travel and trade; and, two, enhance and expand our digital connectivity.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Our air hub has been badly affected by COVID-19 and we are sparing no effort to rebuild it.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: When global passenger traffic resumes, as it surely will, the Changi Air Hub will resume its role at the Global-Asia node, together with all the related sectors such as tourism, manufacturing and logistics.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Accordingly, we must re-establish our position by reopening our borders gradually, positioning Singapore as a safe destination, levelling up capabilities and refreshing our infrastructure.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We are committed to revive our air hub and restore our air connectivity.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: The Multi-Ministry Taskforce is studying this carefully as part of our broader re-opening plans and the Minister for Transport will share more in his Ministerial Statement tomorrow.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Our maritime trade has to date remained resilient to COVID-19, and we will accelerate moves to strengthen our position.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Notwithstanding the 13.5% drop in global trade on a year-on-year basis in the first half of 2020, container throughput at Singapore's ports fell by a milder 1.1% over the same period.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: At the same time, firms are more prepared to diversify their operating bases to increase resilience.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: So, we must press on with improving transhipment capabilities, inking trade facilitation agreements and anchoring key shipping routes through Singapore.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Moving ahead, we will further strengthen our value proposition through greater regional cooperation, and by building up a leading trade and logistics eco-system.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Southeast Asia can benefit from the greater premium on supply chain resilience through regional cooperation.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: For example, the Iskandar Malaysia and Batam, Bintan, Karimun region presents good opportunities for companies to cluster the full value chain of complementary activities from research and development, to regional headquarters and manufacturing.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: To support our ambitions, we will significantly strengthen our entire trade and logistics ecosystem, deepening capabilities in our port, airport and beyond.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We will enhance our infrastructure for Singapore to handle larger flows of food, pharmaceuticals, electronics and e-commerce.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We will accelerate the build-up of digital capabilities, which will be a game-changer for Singapore’s connectivity with Asia and the world.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: It makes the exchange of varied goods and services more efficient, opens up new possibilities, and strengthens our value proposition as a trading node.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: These agreements establish common frameworks and rules for digital trade, enabling our businesses, especially SMEs, to access international markets more easily.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: These moves to enhance Singapore’s digital connectivity will open up new markets and opportunities for our businesses.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: As part of our ITM work, we are helping firms to make full use of digital technology.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: COVID-19 has accelerated the digitalisation and transformation of many businesses, big and small.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: During my dialogue with businesses on Friday, I met the founder of Seonggong, a restaurant group with brands such as Seorae Korean BBQ.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Seonggong used digital technology to revamp its operations, from accounting to ordering to procurement.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: So much so that increased sales from online deliveries have more than offset losses from their dine-in business, by 10%.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: The experience of businesses shows that digitalisation is a strategic capability to unlock growth, evolve their models to harness digital possibilities and to integrate processes such as logistics, payment and marketing.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We will press on with our ITM work, which helps businesses big and small, to transform holistically, bringing together the different aspects needed to upgrade.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: A key priority for us now is to build on this momentum and bring digitalisation to our heartlands.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Senior Minister of State Sim Ann and Minister of State Low Yen Ling will be announcing further plans for heartland enterprises in the coming days.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: I have spoken on seizing new opportunities through physical and digital connectivity.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Beyond being an effective and trusted broker for trade and digital flows, we must be a key node where new ideas are born and nurtured into globally-competitive enterprises.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Today, we have a business-friendly environment, strong rule of law, a skilled and diverse workforce, advanced infrastructure and a globally-competitive eco-system of financial and professional services.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We must continue to build on these complementary strengths built up over the years.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We will be unveiling a new five-year Research, Innovation and Enterprise, or RIE plan in December.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: The plan will build on earlier investments and enhance research to support areas of national priority, such as early childhood development, lifelong learning and keeping our seniors healthy.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We will expand our transformation of the manufacturing, aviation and maritime industries, and deepen our capabilities as a Smart Nation and sustainable society.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We will also position Singapore as a global intellectual property, or IP, centre in Asia.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Ministers Indranee Rajah and Edwin Tong are leading our efforts on our Singapore IP Strategy 2030, and will share details at World IP Day.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: A major effort will be to integrate the work of the Future Economy Council and our RIE plan, so as to accelerate our transformation into an innovation-led economy, powered by technology.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: In this way, our businesses can be more competitive and our workers can have better job prospects.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: An example of how we will scale up the translation of ideas and technology into business improvements is through the use of innovation platforms that bring industry and researchers to work together on specific challenges.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We are also promoting the Open Innovation Network, an online platform which brings problem owners and problem solvers together to create industry-led solutions.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Since 2017, a total of close to $13 million in grant and prize monies has been awarded to firms with viable solutions to deploy and scale their ideas under Enterprise Singapore’s Gov-PACT and IMDA’s Open Innovation Platform.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: This year, we have taken this further, with two rounds of National Innovation Challenges.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We hope to see the outcome of these in the coming months.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: To summarise, we are making good progress in our move to position Singapore as a Global-Asia node of technology, innovation and enterprise.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: By enhancing our connectivity and making innovation pervasive, we can better meet the challenges of a post-COVID world, and create good jobs and a brighter future for all Singaporeans.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Our aim is not just to grow a vibrant, innovative economy, but an inclusive economy, where growth uplifts all Singaporeans.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: To achieve inclusive growth, our workers need to have the skills to stay relevant and we need to provide holistic support to uplift our vulnerable workers.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: To take on good jobs and enjoy the fruits of growth, our workers need the right skills for the job.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We have a strong base of human capital developed through our education system.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: With deep technological changes, skills are going obsolete faster.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We will therefore need extensive upskilling and continual reskilling of our workforce, to equip our workers to continue to get good jobs.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Firms and training providers have a major part to play.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: I urge all firms to make full use of the schemes for developing our people.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
