text: We have a suite of leadership development programmes for Singaporeans at various stages of their careers, such as the Global Ready Talent Programme and the SkillsFuture Leadership Development Initiative.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Companies on the Human Capital Partnership, or HCP Programme, which recognises fair and progressive employers, have also benefited, as the HCP mark endorses them as employers of choice.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We will work closely with industry and training providers, to make sure that the skills workers learn are useful.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Skills upgrading is most effective when the training is relevant to the company’s needs and jobseekers have certainty in the value of the training.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: For example, through NTUC’s Company Training Committees, our Professional Conversion Programmes, or PCPs, and TechSkills Accelerator Company-Led Training programme for ICT jobs.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: As part of this whole-of-society movement to build skills, companies too, need better skills!

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Skills to develop their workers, and redesign skills-based jobs to move beyond paper-based qualifications.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We will continue our work through our ITMs, together with our unions, to drive these changes in each firm and in each sector.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: And finally, individuals have a key part to play in taking charge of their own learning.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We are increasing the digital skills content in our schools and Institutes of Higher Learning to prepare our young for a digital future.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: But learning does not stop after leaving school.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We spend more years outside of school than in school.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: In the process, we can enrich our lives, and our society at large.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Even as we level up the skills of every worker at every age, we still need to bring in global talent to complement our Singapore talent.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Let us all play our part in building a strong, skilled workforce together.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Singaporeans, growing up in a multi-cultural society, have an edge in building relationships with people around the world, especially in a more fragmented post-COVID landscape.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: I have covered how we will grow skills across the workforce to keep our workers competitive.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: The second way to ensure inclusive growth is to help vulnerable and lower wage workers raise their skills and secure good jobs.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: I had a good discussion recently with career coaches and union leaders, to better understand the challenges experienced by different groups of jobseekers.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: For some, it was a skills gap issue.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: For others, it was an issue of expectations – trying to find a job which matched their earlier salary.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: For yet others, especially mid-career and mature executives, employers were concerned about whether they could adapt.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: These are all important issues that we need to tackle together, urgently.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: For example, our lower income workers have been particularly hard hit by COVID-19.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Many of these workers face a twin challenge, as they are also in sectors that will be affected by longer-term structural changes in the economy, such as retail or F&B.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Our middle income and middle-aged workers also have heavy family responsibilities and commitments, but face the challenges of a rapidly evolving labour market.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: For all these workers, there is even more urgency to upskill and transition into jobs with good long-term prospects.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: In the design of our support schemes, we have been deliberate in channelling additional support to vulnerable groups, to help them access opportunities and stay in good jobs.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: For example, mature and older workers are eligible for higher wage support in our career conversion programmes, as well as higher course fee subsidies.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: I announced some of these earlier this year as part of our SkillsFuture Mid-Career Support Package.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: The Progressive Wage Model, or PWM, is an important labour policy innovation.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: PWM is more than a sector-based minimum wage.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: It is a four-in-one framework comprising a Job Ladder, Skills Ladder, Productivity Ladder and Wage Ladder.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: By offering a proper career ladder, skills upgrading ladder, productivity improvement ladder and wage enhancement ladder, our four-in-one PWM transforms jobs that are traditionally less attractive to our locals.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We will expand PWM to more sectors over time, while making sure that businesses in those sectors can absorb this change.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: In doing so, we will raise skill levels and create more and better jobs.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: This will also mean that business costs will go up, which will add to the difficulty of businesses during this time.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: But COVID-19 has highlighted why it is critical, for long-term survival, for firms to be more manpower-lean, productive and have jobs that are attractive to our locals.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We will have to explore solutions and the Government will provide support for the transition.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: It is a continuing journey to improve the job market for our more vulnerable workers.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Beyond incentives, we need to shift culture and employer mindsets.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: But if we focus on the strengths of our workers and adopt flexibility in job design and redesign, we can customise creative solutions for different groups of workers.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: For example, we know that some workers find it hard to travel far for work.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: At the same time, some of the shops in our heartlands may find it difficult to find workers.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Given the scale of structural changes in the global economy, we need to redesign jobs and reskill workers, across all our ITMs, in significant ways.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We need to be innovative in pursuing this and work in close partnerships between employers, workers and our unions.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: It will take time and effort, but if done well, will usher in a more dynamic and inclusive economy.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: I have covered the first and second moves in this next phase of our industry transformation journey.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Our third move is to invest in our economic resilience and sustainability as a source of growth and competitive advantage.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Economic resilience is not a new idea for Singapore.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We have achieved resilience through a diversified economic structure, with multiple engines of growth.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: No one industry accounts for much more than 20% of our GDP, so we do not put all our eggs in one basket.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We thus entered the COVID-19 pandemic on a relatively strong footing.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We were able to ensure sufficient medical supplies and essential goods for our public and healthcare workers because we had a strategic national stockpile in place, supported by a combination of local production of essential supplies, and a diverse network of trading partners.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Beyond essential goods, critical inputs for industrial production and access to workers were cut off due to global work stoppages and travel bans.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Demand also ground to a halt in many industries.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We must therefore act now to improve our economic resilience.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: In doing this, we may have to creatively combine the efficiency of having things ready "just in time" with the resilience of building buffers "just in case".

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Will this drive for resilience come at the expense of growth and efficiency?

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: For example, firms that embrace technology raise not only productivity, but also resilience.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Lingjack, a manufacturer of fire extinguishers, automated its labour-intensive production lines in 2017.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: With over 90% of its production lines automated, Lingjack achieved efficiency gains of up to 40%.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: At the same time, this also made the company less vulnerable to worker shortages during the COVID-19 pandemic.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: One key way to enhance our resilience and to grow is to produce essential supplies locally, which can be used both for local consumption and export.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: One example is medical supplies, such as masks and test kits.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We set ourselves the ambitious "30 by 30" goal of producing 30% of our nutritional needs locally by 2030, up from less than 10% today.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Our agri-food sector will enhance our resilience to food supply disruptions.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: The technology developed in support of this strategy, such as in seeds and alternative proteins, can be exported.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We can grow these capabilities, building on our strengths in R&D and our standing as a trusted hub.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Singapore is already the global R&D centre for AgriProtein, one of the world's leading insect protein companies.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: The R&D team develops technologies to upcycle food waste into sustainable animal feed solutions.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: As we grapple with climate change, environmental sustainability is an important aspect of our economic resilience for a low-carbon and resource-constrained future.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Here again is an opportunity for the green sector to be a growth industry in its own right and to power our economy.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: First, we are transforming our industries to build a sustainable economy.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We will continue to invest in research into energy and resource efficiency technologies and encourage adoption of these technologies through various incentives under EDB, EMA, BCA and NEA.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Going forward, we will further promote the decarbonisation of the economy and pursue initiatives for a more sustainable economy.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Under our Zero Waste Masterplan, we will promote the circular economy and support businesses to turn "trash to treasure", namely, to recycle or transform waste into useful inputs for production.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Harnessing the circular economy model, JTC is working with companies on Jurong Island to build a more sustainable Jurong Island.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We are increasing our deployment of renewable energy sources, such as solar energy, at both the national and industry level.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: And we will invest in new capabilities and solutions, such as hydrogen and carbon capture, utilisation and storage to complement our existing R&D efforts.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: In time, we hope that these promising technologies can become commercially viable decarbonisation pathways in future.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Even as we transform our existing industries, we are seeking new business opportunities in the green economy, given our region's growing needs for sustainable development.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We will establish ourselves as a carbon services hub in Asia.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Efforts to limit the growth of carbon emissions will increase the demand for engineering, legal and consultancy services related to carbon.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: The Alliance for Action for Sustainability is market-testing some concepts and business opportunities.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Finance is also an important enabler of green growth.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We are developing financing solutions and markets in Singapore to help firms finance their adoption of more sustainable practices under MAS' Green Finance Action Plan.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Taken together, our moves to strengthen our economic resilience and sustainability serve a dual purpose.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: They strengthen our economy so that we can bounce back quickly and better from shocks, while adding to our value proposition as a vital global node in Asia.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: In turn, all these initiatives will create many new opportunities and valuable jobs for our people.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: These strategies strengthen both our economy and our social compact.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: The key to achieving our objectives is working together.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: In our system, tripartism – between the Government, businesses and the Labour Movement – has been a tremendous source of strength.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Our Emerging Stronger Taskforce's Alliances for Action are a new form of collaborative partnership – nimble, action-focused partnerships that involve people from a wide spectrum of society, while putting ideas into action quickly.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: This will further strengthen our capacity for economic transformation and change.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: By working together, our businesses will be better positioned to capture new opportunities in Asia, digitalisation, innovation and to build a more resilient and sustainable economy.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Our people will be better placed to take on these new opportunities and bounce back from setbacks.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We can then emerge from this pandemic stronger as an economy, as a society and as one people.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: The proposed reallocations are indicated in the Supplementary Estimates presented to Parliament today.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: When I announced the Fortitude Budget just after the start of the financial year, the economic situation and overall revenue picture were highly uncertain.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We are now in the middle of the financial year and are in a better position to revise the overall revenue estimates.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Hence, I am presenting the revised revenue estimates to Parliament, which will also take into account the revenue forgone arising from measures in the Fortitude Budget.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: There is no additional draw for this latest support package itself.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: When I briefed the President and the Council of Presidential Advisers in August, I thanked them for their earlier support and approval for the use of Past Reserves to fund our response to COVID-19.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We are starting this new term of Government from a most challenging fiscal position.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: For this financial year, we already expect operating revenues to be 16% lower than initial estimates presented at the Unity Budget in February 2020.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We expect our revenue position to be weak for a number of years, as the effects of COVID-19 on the global economy linger and our economy slows.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: At the same time, our expenditure will rise as we continue to provide support for our people and businesses.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: In short, the Government is bearing a substantial part of the economy-wide adjustment during this crisis, through reduced revenues and substantial transfers to households and businesses.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: This challenging fiscal position is a result of a global pandemic that no one could have predicted.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: As we do so, we must be careful not to spend in a way that squanders what generations before us have painstakingly built up.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We will continue to invest decisively in our national priorities, with a deep commitment to leave behind a better future for our children.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: There is much work to be done to transform our economy, and to build a fair and inclusive society, a sustainable and liveable city, and a safe and secure Singapore.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We will have to find ways to fund these sustainably – higher taxes, and more effective spending.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: These are difficult choices, but we must meet them head-on.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We will pay for our recurrent needs, like healthcare spending, with recurrent revenues, such as taxes.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We will also maintain a disciplined and judicious use of borrowing, reserving its use for long-term infrastructure whose benefits are spread across many generations.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Our Past Reserves have been critical in our fight against COVID-19.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Governments around the world have committed trillions of dollars in response to COVID-19, and their debt levels have risen to record highs.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Such debt will take generations to pay off.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We have avoided this outcome because successive generations have built up strong reserves ahead of this crisis.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We must have the discipline to start earning, saving, and investing for the future again.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: COVID-19 is not our first crisis and certainly will not be the last.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: (In Mandarin):   The COVID-19 situation in Singapore has stabilised.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: The key to controlling the pandemic is Singaporeans working together.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We must remain vigilant and continue to cooperate in disease prevention and comply with the safe distancing measures.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Testing, tracing, development and production of vaccines as well as the progress of controlling the pandemic in other countries will determine when we can safely reopen all our economic activities.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: At present, the pace of recovery varies across sectors.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Hence, we will continue to provide assistance to Singaporeans and businesses from now till the next financial year or beyond.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: The Monetary Authority of Singapore (MAS) will also extend the MAS Singapore Dollar Facility for Enterprise Singapore Loans to help businesses continue to access credit.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: In addition, we will extend the Enhanced Training Support Package to June 2021 to provide course fee subsidies to hardest-hit sectors such as aviation and tourism.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We understand that the uncertainty brought about by the pandemic has caused many young families to postpone their parenthood plans.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Hence, we will provide eligible couples with a one-off additional support to help them reduce their child-rearing burden.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: The Government has started to draw up the Budget for 2021.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We will continue to work closely with businesses, workers and community organisations to chart the way forward for Singapore.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: In order to create more quality jobs for our people, we need a flourishing economy.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Fortunately, the Government has already started on industry transformation with the setting up of the Future Economy Council and introduced the Industry Transformation Maps for the various sectors.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We have also established the Emerging Stronger Taskforce to refresh our economic strategy to prepare for the post-COVID era.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We have also established the Alliances for Action to try out new ideas.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We also need to further consolidate Singapore's position as a Global-Asia node of technology, innovation, and enterprise .

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We must invest in economic resilience and sustainability as a source of competitive advantage to prepare for a sustainable low-carbon future.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Our workers need to have skills to stay relevant.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We will expand the Progressive Wage Model to more sectors over time, introduce job redesign and raise the skills of our workers to benefit more groups of lower-wage workers.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: And in time, we will slow down the growth of foreign workers in these sectors.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: In the Ministerial Statement I made in August, I have provided an additional $8 billion to fight the COVID-19 pandemic.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Together with the four Budgets announced earlier, we have promised as much as $100 billion to help our people and businesses to tide over this difficult time.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Besides having to meet huge expenditures, our tax revenue is also facing substantial pressure due to economic slowdown globally.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: A thriving economy not only enables Singaporeans to realise their aspirations but also ensures that the Government has sufficient resources to meet their needs.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: The post-COVID era will be a very different world.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We will constantly refine our economic strategies to keep up with the times, innovate and maintain our competitive advantage.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: No matter how challenging the situations will be, we will put the interests and welfare of Singaporeans first.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: I believe that as long as we stay united, we will be able to overcome our immediate difficulties and usher in a better future.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: (In English): Mr Speaker, our people and businesses are in the thick of battling COVID-19.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We have adapted together, and I am glad that many continue to give their utmost in this difficult situation, and do their best for their families and communities.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Given the great uncertainty ahead, we have to remain vigilant, work in close partnership, and continue to adapt as we plan and move ahead.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: I encourage each of you to share with us your perspectives and ideas, and to do your part to build our future as part of our Singapore Together movement.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Together, we will overcome this crisis and emerge stronger.
